outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solution_passed flags are false, so there is no pass/fail-discordant official outcome. The material quality gap is 0/171 versus 53/171. Parallel used two advisory subagents, but they completed and returned review checklists; the parent owned all writes and final integration. The strongest concrete difference is ordinary implementation and verification coverage: serial added verifiers/mock_openai_client.py and smoke-tested MockAsyncOpenAI through the package export, while parallel exposed only the root mock_openai_client.py in the artifact and reported local pytest/compileall without that smoke check.
parallel_contributors: Parallel final artifact exposed root mock_openai_client.py but not an observed package-level verifiers/mock_openai_client.py.
Parallel relied on local self-authored tests and compileall, which did not catch the evaluator-facing API surface gap.
serial_contributors: Serial added verifiers/mock_openai_client.py and root mock_openai_client.py in the implementation path.
Serial ran an import smoke test importing MockAsyncOpenAI from verifiers and the root module before finalization.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The package-level mock-client module/export difference is an ordinary implementation coverage difference, not a proven coordination or handoff failure.
Both runs failed overall because neither implementation satisfied the full 171-test official suite, and both relied on local tests after the submit tool was unavailable.
evaluator_effects: Only completed official counts and summary are available inside the pair; the exact official failure trace is not present, so the package-mock explanation is supported but not exclusive.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors to a material quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a retained concurrency pattern

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly kept implementation ownership after spawning review-only children and then applied the main implementation patch itself, so implementation was not ownerless.
There were no separately owned child implementations requiring a missing integrator; the parent alone integrated its package files.
The parent owned final assembly and produced the final workspace artifact; no assembled candidate was left without an owner.
The parent tracked implementation, tests, cleanup, and final response as one pipeline, so no end-to-end pipeline ownership gap is visible.
No mandatory serial harness or oracle blocked productive work; the child reviews were advisory and the parent proceeded after ordinary setup.

Although two reviewers ran first, their reports returned and the parent completed implementation and local verification; the evidence does not show deadline pressure or incomplete work caused by that investigation phase.
The indispensable implementation path stayed with the parent and received most of the work; the failed score is better explained by API coverage choices than capacity starvation.
Only two advisory children were spawned, both completed early, and the parent had time for implementation, repeated pytest runs, compileall, cleanup, and finalization.
Neither child received a broad implementation deliverable; both had bounded review/checklist scopes and returned completed findings.
The visible parent message described review-only scopes, and the encrypted child briefs do not prove an already-known implementation or delivery requirement was omitted from a child deliverable.
The parent did not delegate separately implemented components expected to interoperate, so there was no missing cross-agent interface contract.
No known finding is shown disappearing between child and parent; the returned checklists reached the parent.
The child handoffs were concise checklists, and the parent visibly acted on several items rather than being unable to reduce them.
The returned reviews were not based on superseded workspace state that the parent later consumed as current.
The two completed review reports did not give incompatible contracts that remained unresolved at integration time.

The parent closed after local tests and official evaluation later failed, but no non-evaluator evidence shows a parent-visible integrated acceptance gap before closure; serial also relied on local verification, making this an ordinary verification limitation rather than a parallel-specific pattern.
No replacement or retry child was spawned, so there is no repeated-work retry without inherited checkpoint state.
